newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on deliveries, Australia.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on deliveries, Australia.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on the posting Tuesday of 700,000 bushels of wheat notices for delivery on the December contract, traders said.
"December wheat is under pressure on deliveries and the Australian wheat crop," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics said Tuesday the 1996-97 Australian wheat crop would total 21.3 million tonnes, up from the previous forecast of 20.9 million.
Traders also said the wheat market was pressed by nearly ideal weather for the 1997 U.S. winter wheat crop.
USDA Monday said 75 percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in good to excellent condition as of Sunday, up from 74 percent in that category the previous week.
The wheat market also took note of news Bangladesh bought 100,000 tonnes of wheat and U.S. exporters said the deal probably was struck with Australia rather than the U.S.
European grain traders overnight said Tunisia was in the market Tuesday for 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat for January and February shipment.
Wheat closed 8-1/4 cents lower to 1/2 cent higher, with December down 8-1/4 at $3.85 per bushel.

Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures said the deliveries indeed pressured the market. But the bottom line for wheat was the dimming hope for significant sales abroad of U.S. wheat soon.
"There's no light at the end of the tunnel for the U.S. to sell wheat to anybody," Searcy said.
U.S. wheat prices remain uncompetitive with other world wheat producers and the outlook for a change soon in that scenario does not look rosy.
"There's a big Australian crop and they're going to have wheat left over, Australia and probably the EU too," he said. "There's just no good news.
Commercials were on both sides of the market with Cargill Inc a purchaser of three million bushels of March and a seller of 1.5 million March, traders said.
Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought six million March and sold 4.5 million March, Refco Inc and SAK Futures each sold 1.5 million March, traders said.
Term Commodities spread one million March/July at 39 cents, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000, above the 11,295 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Smith Barney sold 550 March $3.80 puts at 15 cents, Produce Grain sold 200 March $3.60 puts at 9-1/2 cents and Dean Witter Reynolds sold 250 July $3.50 calls at 13 to 14 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000, below the 5,800 contracts traded Monday.
